title: Chain validators with decorators

blocks.text: The page's second pitfall is a validator that is edited for every new rule:

Its fix is the Decorator pattern: **each decorator implements the same `Validator` interface as the validator it wraps, asks that validator first, and adds its own rule**. No validator is ever edited to add a rule. In `Checks`, write:

items: `NonNullValidator`: valid when the value is not null;
`NonEmptyValidator(delegate)`: valid when the delegate says valid and the value is not empty (`"  "` is not empty);
`MinLengthValidator(delegate, min)`: valid when the delegate says valid and the value has at least `min` characters, spaces included (`value.length()`, nothing trimmed).

blocks.text: Each decorator **always asks its delegate first**, with the same value, and only then applies its own rule.

Validator<String> validator = new MinLengthValidator(
    new NonEmptyValidator(new NonNullValidator()), 5);

which rejects `null`, `""` and `"abc"` and accepts `"hello"`. A decorator wraps **any** `Validator<String>`, including a lambda written later, so `new MinLengthValidator(v -> v != null && v.startsWith("A"), 3)` accepts `"Anna"` and rejects `"Bob12"`.

cases.says: The page's chain rejects "" and "abc" and accepts "hello".
null is rejected by every chain, because each decorator asks its delegate before looking at the value.
Wrapping a lambda that wants a leading A keeps that rule: "Bob12" is rejected.
Length is value.length(): two emoji are four chars, so they pass a minimum of 4.

origin.section: 8.1.2.3. Extending Behavior Without Modifying Existing Code

concepts: A decorator implements the same interface as the object it wraps and delegates to it, so validation rules are added without editing any validator.
